sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
The Dragolink API is a comprehensive suite of RESTful services designed to help you integrate link management, analytics, and QR code generation directly into your own applications.

Our API is built on standard REST principles. All URLs are predictable and resource-oriented. The API accepts standard form-encoded requests as well as JSON payloads, and returns JSON-encoded responses. We use standard HTTP response codes to indicate success or failure.

alert.title: API Versioning
alert.message: When we make backwards-incompatible changes to the API, we release new dated versions. The current version is 2024-01-01. You can pin your API version via the Dragolink-Version HTTP header.

sections.title: Authentication
sections.content:
The Dragolink API uses API keys to authenticate requests. You can view and manage your API keys in the Dragolink Dashboard under Developer Settings.

Authentication to the API is performed via HTTP Bearer Auth. You must provide your API key in the Authorization header of every request.

alert.title: Keep your keys safe
alert.message: Your API keys carry full privileges to your account. Do not share your secret API keys in publicly accessible areas such as GitHub, client-side code, or public forums. If a key is compromised, roll it immediately in the dashboard.

sections.title: Links API
sections.content: The Links API forms the core of Dragolink. Use these endpoints to programmatically shorten long URLs, assign custom aliases, organize links with tags, and set expiration parameters.

endpoints.title: Create a Link
endpoints.description: Creates a new short URL. You can optionally provide a custom alias, set an expiration date, and generate a QR code simultaneously.

parameters.name: destination
parameters.description: The long URL that you want to shorten. Must be a valid URL starting with http:// or https://.

parameters.name: domain_id
parameters.description: The ID of the custom domain to use for the short link. If omitted, the default dragolink.com domain is used.

parameters.name: alias
parameters.description: A custom short back-half (e.g., 'summer-sale'). Leave blank for a randomly generated string.

parameters.name: expires_at
parameters.description: ISO 8601 timestamp for when the link should expire (e.g., '2024-12-31T23:59:59Z').

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Protect the destination URL with a password.

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description: An array of string tags used to organize and filter links.

endpoints.title: Retrieve a Link
endpoints.description: Retrieves the details of an existing short link. You need to supply the unique link identifier that was returned upon creation.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the link.

endpoints.title: Update a Link
endpoints.description: Updates an existing short link. You can change the destination, update the expiration date, or modify tags. The short alias cannot be changed once created.

endpoints.title: Delete a Link
endpoints.description: Permanently deletes a short link. It will no longer redirect to the destination URL and will immediately return a 404 Not Found to visitors.

sections.title: Analytics API
sections.content: The Analytics API allows you to retrieve highly detailed metrics about your links. You can query data by time series, geographic locations, device types, and referrers.

endpoints.title: Get Link Clicks (Time Series)
endpoints.description: Retrieves a time-series array of clicks for a specific link over a given timeframe. Data is aggregated by hour, day, or month depending on the interval parameter.

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description: ISO 8601 timestamp for the beginning of the reporting period.

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: ISO 8601 timestamp for the end of the reporting period.

parameters.name: interval
parameters.description: The aggregation interval. Options: 'hour', 'day', 'month'. Defaults to 'day'.

endpoints.title: Get Geographic Data
endpoints.description: Retrieves the distribution of clicks mapped to visitor countries and cities.

endpoints.title: Get Referrer Data
endpoints.description: Retrieves the distribution of clicks mapped to traffic sources (e.g., Twitter, Google, Direct).

sections.title: QR Codes API
sections.content: Generate and manage dynamic QR codes. Dynamic QR codes can have their destination URL changed at any time without needing to reprint the physical code.

endpoints.title: Generate a QR Code
endpoints.description: Creates a new dynamic QR code associated with an existing link.

parameters.name: fg_color
parameters.description: The foreground color of the QR code in Hex format (e.g., '#000000').

parameters.name: bg_color
parameters.description: The background color of the QR code in Hex format (e.g., '#FFFFFF').

parameters.name: logo_url
parameters.description: A URL to a small image to embed in the center of the QR code.

sections.title: Webhooks API
sections.content: Dragolink can send webhook events that notify your application any time an event happens on your account. This is especially useful for asynchronous events—like a link being clicked or a QR code being scanned—that are not triggered by a direct API request.

endpoints.title: Create a Webhook
endpoints.description: Registers a new webhook endpoint to receive real-time event payloads.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: The HTTPS URL where Dragolink should send the webhook payloads.

parameters.name: events
parameters.description: An array of event types to subscribe to (e.g., ['link.clicked', 'qr.scanned']).

parameters.name: secret
parameters.description: A custom cryptographic secret used to sign the webhook payloads. If omitted, one is generated automatically.

endpoints.title: List Webhooks
endpoints.description: Returns a list of all active webhook endpoints on your account.

sections.title: Errors
sections.content:
Dragolink uses conventional HTTP response codes to indicate the success or failure of an API request. 

In general:
- Codes in the 2xx range indicate success.
- Codes in the 4xx range indicate an error that failed given the information provided (e.g., a required parameter was omitted, a charge failed, etc.).
- Codes in the 5xx range indicate an error with Dragolink's servers.

errorsList.description: The request was unacceptable, often due to missing a required parameter.
The parameters were valid but the request failed (e.g., rate limit exceeded or payment required).
The API key doesn't have permissions to perform the request.
The request conflicts with another request (e.g., custom alias is already taken).
Too many requests hit the API too quickly. We recommend an exponential backoff of your requests.
Something went wrong on Dragolink's end. (These are rare.)
